title: Incomplete dominance and codominance
notes: Not all traits follow simple dominant-recessive patterns.
- Example: Snapdragon flowers - Red (RR) x White (WW) -> Pink (RW)
- Both alleles are fully expressed in heterozygote
- Example: ABO blood groups - IA and IB are codominant
- Example: Roan cattle - red and white hairs both appear
- More than two alleles exist for a gene in the population
- Individual still has only two alleles
- Example: ABO blood groups - IA, IB, i (three alleles)
- Anti-A antibodies in type B and O; Anti-B antibodies in type A and O
Distinguish incomplete dominance vs codominance; Solve blood group crosses.
confusion: x Incomplete dominance = blending. x It's not permanent blending - alleles remain distinct.
x Codominance = incomplete dominance. x In codominance both show fully, not intermediate.
x Type AB can donate to anyone. x Type AB can ONLY receive, not donate.
practice: Cross red snapdragon (RR) with white (WW). What are F1 and F2 ratios?
A type A father and type B mother have a type O child. What are parent genotypes?
Can a type AB parent and type O parent have a type O child? Why/why not?
Explain why codominance differs from incomplete dominance.
